questions.q: Can I give you a piece of *___*?
questions.explain: *advice* is the uncountable noun; *advise* is the verb.

questions.q: The new law will *___* thousands of people.
questions.explain: *affect* is the verb (influence); *effect* is usually the noun (result).

questions.q: She's *___* to Spain. She'll be back next week.
questions.explain: *gone* = she went and is still there; *been* = she went and came back.

questions.q: Could you *___* me your pen for a minute?
questions.explain: You *lend* something to someone; you *borrow* it from them.

questions.q: He *___* me that he was leaving.
questions.explain: *tell* takes a person as the direct object; *say* doesn't (*said to me*).

questions.q: I've lived here *___* 2019.
questions.explain: *since* + a point in time; *for* + a period.

questions.q: I fell asleep *___* the film.
questions.explain: *during* + noun tells us when; *while* needs a clause.

questions.q: You need to *___* a decision soon.
questions.explain: We *make* a decision, a mistake, a plan; we *do* homework, a job.

questions.q: *___* students have to wear a uniform.
questions.explain: *all* + plural noun; *every* and *each* take a singular noun.

questions.q: Prices *___* by 10% last year.
questions.explain: *rise – rose – risen* has no object; *raise* needs one (*they raised prices*).

questions.q: Please *___* me to buy milk.
questions.explain: Someone *reminds* you to do something; you *remember* it yourself.

questions.q: Thieves *___* the bank last night.
questions.explain: You *rob* a person or place; you *steal* a thing.

questions.q: It was *___* a good party that nobody wanted to leave.
questions.explain: *such (a/an)* + (adjective +) noun; *so* + adjective alone.

questions.q: The dog hurt *___* leg.
questions.explain: *its* (no apostrophe) is the possessive; *it's* = it is / it has.

questions.q: There were *___* people at the meeting than last time.
questions.explain: In careful English, *fewer* goes with plural countable nouns.

questions.q: I *___* my umbrella on the bus.
questions.explain: When you name the place, use *leave*, not *forget*.

questions.q: The party was great *___*!
questions.explain: *fun* = enjoyable; *funny* = makes you laugh.

questions.q: I don't know *___* to accept the job or not.
questions.explain: Before a *to*-infinitive, use *whether*, not *if*.

questions.q: She works *___* a nurse at the city hospital.
questions.explain: *as* + noun = in the role of; *like* = similar to.

questions.q: Could you *___* the newspaper from the kitchen?
questions.explain: *fetch* = go, get something and bring it back.

questions.q: *___* we waited for an hour, the bus came.
questions.explain: *at last* = after a long wait, with relief. *Lastly* introduces the last item in a list.

questions.q: I'm so *___* to you for all your help.
questions.explain: We are *grateful to* people for what they did; *thankful* is for lucky situations.

questions.q: She's my *___* sister — she's two years older than me.
questions.explain: *elder* is used before a noun for family members (but *older than*, never *elder than*).

questions.q: *___* is your new teacher like?
questions.explain: *What is … like?* asks for a description; *How is …?* asks about health or progress.

questions.q: I had the *___* to work in Canada last year.
questions.explain: An *opportunity* is a chance to do something; a *possibility* is something that might happen.
